findings.current: *Oh. This time, maybe I’ll be able to save the Captain.*
findings.defect: Mujin says this to the narrator; italics turn it into an unspoken thought and obscure who is speaking.
findings.rationale: The line follows Mujin looking directly at him and speaking, and ends by identifying it as the thought Mujin had.
findings.replacement: “Oh, I thought, maybe this time I can be the one to save you, Captain.”
findings.source: “아, 이번만큼은 내가 조장님을 구해 줄 수도 있겠구나, 하는 생각이요.”

findings.current: Then this time, wouldn’t even a lowlife like me be useful?
findings.defect: “Lowlife” suggests bad character rather than inferior martial skill.
findings.rationale: 하수 describes someone less skilled than the masters he has just mentioned.
findings.replacement: Then this time, couldn’t even a low-level fighter like me be useful?
findings.source: 그럼 이번만큼은 저 같은 하수도 도움이 되지 않겠어요?

findings.current: Keep this up and I might get fed up and return to the family estate on my own.
findings.defect: “The family estate” leaves which family he serves unclear and suggests a property rather than his return to the Jin Family.
findings.rationale: His mock threat is to stop accompanying the Captain and return to 본가, the family he serves.
findings.replacement: Keep this up and I might get fed up and head back to the Jin Family on my own.
findings.source: 계속 이러시면 저도 수틀려서 혼자 본가로 복귀하는 수가 있습니다.

findings.current: But that could take a while. In a situation like this, it doesn’t feel right to leave you behind. You’re not in your usual condition, either.
findings.defect: The draft drops “longer than expected” and changes Mujin’s concern about being away from his post into a statement about leaving the Captain behind.
findings.rationale: 생각보다 marks a comparison with his expectation; 자리를 비우는 건 concerns his absence during the crisis.
findings.replacement: But that’s longer than I expected. Being away at a time like this is a bit… And you’re not in your usual condition, either.
findings.source: 하지만 생각보다 오래 걸리는데요. 지금 같은 상황에서 자리를 비우는 건 좀…… 조장님 몸 상태도 평소 같지 않으시잖아요.

findings.current: It was something I’d prepared two days ago, but had hesitated to take out until the very end.
findings.defect: “Hesitated to take out until the very end” implies a delay; he was undecided whether to take out the note at all.
findings.rationale: 꺼낼까 말까 expresses a choice between taking it out and not taking it out.
findings.replacement: I’d prepared it two days ago, but until the last moment, I’d wavered over whether to take it out at all.
findings.source: 이미 이틀 전 준비해 두었던, 마지막까지 꺼낼까 말까 망설였던 물건이었다.

findings.current: In a dangerous gamble where no one knows what will happen, you must want to save as many people as you can.
findings.defect: The generalized “as many people as you can” loses Hong Jin’s pointed “even one more person,” which bears on why the Captain sent people away.
findings.rationale: 한 명이라도 더 emphasizes the value of saving one additional life.
findings.replacement: In a dangerous gamble where no one knows what will happen, you must want to save even one more person.
findings.source: 어떻게 될지 모르는 이 위험한 도박판에서, 한 명이라도 더 살리고 싶을 테니까.

findings.current: They say humans are creatures of habit.
findings.defect: “Habit” shifts the opening claim from adaptation to routine.
findings.rationale: 적응 is adaptation; the opening sets up what repeated experience still cannot make familiar.
findings.replacement: Someone once said humans are creatures of adaptation.

findings.current:
“Right, I was a shrike worrying about a Heavenly Eagle.”

“Usually, it’d be a crane you were worried about, not a Heavenly Eagle.”
findings.defect: Both birds in the altered idiom are misidentified: 뱁새 is a crow-tit, and 황새 is a stork.
findings.rationale: The Captain’s correction depends on the familiar crow-tit-and-stork pairing; Mujin has substituted the grander Heavenly Eagle.
findings.replacement:
“Right, I was a crow-tit worrying about a Heavenly Eagle.”

“Usually, it’d be a stork you were worried about, not a Heavenly Eagle.”
findings.source:
“하긴, 뱁새가 천응(天鷹)을 걱정했네요.”

“보통은 천응이 아니라 황새일 텐데.”

findings.current: If you can move your eyes properly, you’re already halfway there.
findings.defect: “Move your eyes properly” sounds like an eye-movement technique rather than watching an opponent while under attack.
findings.rationale: The advice follows Mujin shutting his eyes against an expected blow.
findings.replacement: Even just keeping your eyes on your opponent puts you halfway there.
findings.source: 눈깔만 제대로 굴려도 절반은 먹고 들어가니까.

summary: The draft is broadly faithful, but one spoken line becomes an unspoken thought, and several choices alter characterization or obscure the decision to send the pavilion away.
